reverie.title: REVERIE — the field where speech learned its own name
narr: You stand with Katita in a field at first light. She points:
"Listen. The birds aren't singing yet. What you hear is the
silence learning to break itself." Her hand finds yours. The
air tastes like copper, like the inside of your own throat,
like standing at the exact moment breath becomes vowel.
"The archive," she says, "is just the field learning to speak."

exits.label: back toward the silences, the dark before utterance
further into the field, where other first sounds gather and compare
downward into the root-chambers where words still sleep before they learn to speak
out toward the horizon where the first speech still echoes
